## Fingerprint canonical form

Finding fingerprints are `SHA-256` over a domain-separated, versioned canonical form (`schema=1`) containing the detector kind, surface, repository-relative POSIX path, affected feature and an optional detector-supplied stable key.

Line numbers, notebook cells, explanatory detail, timestamps and observed counts are excluded, so moving a finding to another line or rewording its message keeps the same identity. Moving the file, changing the detector kind, changing the affected feature or changing the stable key changes the fingerprint. Dataset and split columns are always treated as features, even when they contain `/` or `:1`. The bundled code scanners derive the stable key from the offending construct's structural AST shape and enclosing function/class (with a deterministic suffix for identical repeats), so repeated findings of one kind in a file stay distinct and the key contains no line number, message text or machine path.

### missingness_target_signal

- Surface: `dataset`
- Default severity: `medium`
- Scored: yes
- Requires: nothing
- Modalities: tabular
- Advice key: `missingness_target_signal`
- Benchmark case: `binary target association`
- Introduced: 0.13.0
- Anchor: `#missingness_target_signal`

Investigate why the value is missing. If missingness is caused by the outcome, a labelling process or a post-outcome system, do not use the column or a missing-value indicator. Otherwise confirm the indicator is available before prediction and compare a model with and without it.

### missingness_group_signal

- Surface: `dataset`
- Default severity: `low`
- Scored: yes
- Requires: nothing
- Modalities: tabular
- Advice key: `missingness_group_signal`
- Benchmark case: `group-associated missingness`
- Introduced: 0.13.0
- Anchor: `#missingness_group_signal`

Check whether groups differ in how values are recorded. If group membership is unavailable at prediction time, avoid features whose missingness depends on it; otherwise split by group and document the collection difference.

- Benchmark case: `StandardScaler fitted before split`
- Introduced: 0.13.0
- Anchor: `#preprocess_before_split`

Split first, then fit on the training part only. Wrap the steps in sklearn.pipeline.Pipeline and fit/cross-validate the pipeline.

### fit_on_full_data

- Surface: `code`
- Default severity: `medium`
- Scored: yes
- Requires: nothing
- Modalities: code
- Advice key: `fit_on_full_data`
- Benchmark case: `scaler fitted on full X after split`
- Introduced: 0.13.0
- Anchor: `#fit_on_full_data`

Fit on the training split only (X_train). If this is the final refit after evaluation it is fine; otherwise put the steps in a Pipeline.

### future_target_feature_before_split

- Surface: `code`
- Default severity: `high`
- Scored: yes
- Requires: nothing
- Modalities: code
- Advice key: `future_target_feature_before_split`
- Benchmark case: `negative target shift before split`
- Introduced: 0.13.0
- Anchor: `#future_target_feature_before_split`

Do not build features from future target values. Use only information available at prediction time; for time series, construct lag features from past observations and split chronologically.

### get_dummies_before_split

- Surface: `code`
- Default severity: `low`
- Scored: yes
- Requires: nothing
- Modalities: code
- Advice key: `get_dummies_before_split`
- Benchmark case: `get_dummies before split`
- Introduced: 0.13.0
- Anchor: `#get_dummies_before_split`

Split first, then fit a OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown='ignore') on the training data inside a sklearn Pipeline so held-out categories do not shape the encoding.

### fillna_before_split

- Surface: `code`
- Default severity: `medium`
- Scored: yes
- Requires: nothing
- Modalities: code
- Advice key: `fillna_before_split`
- Benchmark case: `fillna with full-data mean before split`
- Introduced: 0.13.0
- Anchor: `#fillna_before_split`

Impute using training data only: split first, then compute the mean/median on the training split and apply it to both splits, or use SimpleImputer inside a Pipeline.

### manual_scale_before_split

- Surface: `code`
- Default severity: `high`
- Scored: yes
- Requires: nothing
- Modalities: code
- Advice key: `manual_scale_before_split`
- Benchmark case: `z-score by hand before split`
- Introduced: 0.13.0
- Anchor: `#manual_scale_before_split`

Compute the statistics (mean, std, min, max, ...) on the training split only and apply them to the test split, or use a scaler inside a Pipeline so held-out rows never help set the scale.

### group_stat_before_split

- Surface: `code`
- Default severity: `medium`
- Scored: yes
- Requires: nothing
- Modalities: code
- Advice key: `group_stat_before_split`
- Benchmark case: `groupby agg into a column before split`
- Introduced: 0.13.0
- Anchor: `#group_stat_before_split`

Compute group statistics on the training split only, or wrap the encoding in a Pipeline and evaluate with cross-validation.

### frequency_encode_before_split

- Surface: `code`
- Default severity: `low`
- Scored: yes
- Requires: nothing
- Modalities: code
- Advice key: `frequency_encode_before_split`
- Benchmark case: `frequency encoding from all rows before split`
- Introduced: 0.13.0
- Anchor: `#frequency_encode_before_split`

Compute category frequencies from the training split only and map them onto both splits, or use a Pipeline encoder fitted on X_train.

### temporal_split_shuffle

- Surface: `code`
- Default severity: `medium`
- Scored: yes
- Requires: nothing
- Modalities: code
- Advice key: `temporal_split_shuffle`
- Benchmark case: `time-sorted frame split with default shuffle`
- Introduced: 0.13.0
- Anchor: `#temporal_split_shuffle`

Split time-ordered data chronologically (shuffle=False, or a time-based split) so future rows never enter the training set.

### no_random_state

- Surface: `code`
- Default severity: `low`
- Scored: yes
- Requires: nothing
- Modalities: code
- Advice key: `no_random_state`
- Benchmark case: `train_test_split without random_state`
- Introduced: 0.13.0
- Anchor: `#no_random_state`

Set an explicit seed wherever randomness enters the run (random_state=<int> in scikit-learn, seed=<int> in XGBoost/LightGBM/PyTorch, or the equivalent framework argument) and record it in the pipeline metadata so the run can be reproduced.

### no_stratify

- Surface: `code`
- Default severity: `low`
- Scored: yes
- Requires: nothing
- Modalities: code
- Advice key: `no_stratify`
- Benchmark case: `train_test_split without stratify`
- Introduced: 0.13.0
- Anchor: `#no_stratify`

Pass stratify=<labels> to train_test_split for classification targets so the train and test splits keep the overall class ratio; without it, an imbalanced target can land mostly in one split and distort the evaluation.

### pipeline_split_overlap

- Surface: `code`
- Default severity: `high`
- Scored: no
- Requires: nothing
- Modalities: code
- Advice key: `pipeline_split_overlap`
- Benchmark case: `train and eval share one dataset`
- Introduced: 0.13.0
- Anchor: `#pipeline_split_overlap`

Make the evaluation inputs independent of the training run: split the source data once into disjoint train/eval artifacts, and have the evaluation stage read only the eval artifact. Never point an eval stage at a training stage output or at the same raw input the training stage consumed.

### pipeline_unresolved_lineage

- Surface: `code`
- Default severity: `low`
- Scored: no
- Requires: nothing
- Modalities: code
- Advice key: `pipeline_unresolved_lineage`
- Benchmark case: `unresolved stage dependency`
- Introduced: 0.13.0
- Anchor: `#pipeline_unresolved_lineage`

Fix the dependency path or add the stage that produces it, then re-run the pipeline audit. Until the producer is resolved, do not treat this dependency as verified lineage.

### pipeline_param_drift

- Surface: `code`
- Default severity: `low`
- Scored: no
- Requires: nothing
- Modalities: code
- Advice key: `pipeline_param_drift`
- Benchmark case: `locked parameter drift`

- Anchor: `#pipeline_param_drift`

Re-run the pipeline (or commit the new lock) so dvc.lock and the parameter files agree, and keep parameter changes in the same commit as the run they produced.

### pipeline_missing_digest

- Surface: `code`
- Default severity: `low`
- Scored: no
- Requires: nothing
- Modalities: code
- Advice key: `pipeline_missing_digest`
- Benchmark case: `locked output without digest`
- Introduced: 0.13.0
- Anchor: `#pipeline_missing_digest`

Re-run the stage so the lock records an md5/hash for every output, and commit the lock. Without a digest the artifact cannot be tied to the evaluated model.

### pipeline_unpinned_dependency

- Surface: `code`
- Default severity: `low`
- Scored: no
- Requires: nothing
- Modalities: code
- Advice key: `pipeline_unpinned_dependency`
- Benchmark case: `unpinned requirements entry`

Pin exact versions (package==version) in the requirements file, or record them in a lock file, so re-running the pipeline installs the same environment.
